title: Uttarakhand Hill Stations Itinerary: Mussoorie, Nainital and Kumaon
seoTitle: Uttarakhand Hill Stations Itinerary: Garhwal and Kumaon | Kudozz Club
metaDescription: Two Uttarakhand hill-station itineraries: Rishikesh, Mussoorie and Dhanaulti in Garhwal, and Nainital, Mukteshwar, Kausani and Binsar in Kumaon, day by day.
description: Two practical Uttarakhand hill-station itineraries: a five-day Garhwal route through Rishikesh, Mussoorie, Landour and Dhanaulti, and a seven-day Kumaon loop through Nainital, Bhimtal, Mukteshwar, Kausani and Binsar, with how to combine them, trains from Delhi, seasons and monsoon cautions.
dek: Uttarakhand's hills divide naturally into Garhwal and Kumaon. Here are two routes, and how to join them if you have more time.

hero.alt: Snow on a church in Mussoorie

intro: Garhwal and Kumaon are close on the map but far apart by road, so most trips pick one. Garhwal, reached via Dehradun, combines Rishikesh with the ridge towns of Mussoorie, Landour and Dhanaulti. Kumaon, reached via Kathgodam, links the lake district around Nainital with ridge villages such as Mukteshwar, Kausani and Binsar that face the high Himalaya.
Both routes suit March to June and October to December. In the monsoon, landslides are common, so keep drives short and flexible.
quickAnswer: Two good Uttarakhand hill-station itineraries: a five-day Garhwal route (Rishikesh, then Mussoorie and Landour, with a day at Dhanaulti) via Dehradun; and a seven-day Kumaon loop (Nainital and Bhimtal, Mukteshwar, Kausani and Binsar) via Kathgodam. Combining both takes about 11 to 12 days. The best months are March to June and October to December; avoid long drives in the monsoon.
takeaways: Garhwal is reached via Dehradun or Haridwar; Kumaon via Kathgodam.
Mussoorie and Landour suit walkers; Kumaon's ridges suit view-seekers.
Kausani, Mukteshwar and Binsar face Nanda Devi, Trisul and Panchachuli in clear weather.
October to December has the clearest views.
Combining Garhwal and Kumaon needs a long transfer day.

sections.heading: Combining both
paras: To see Garhwal and Kumaon together, allow 11 to 12 days and plan a long transfer between Mussoorie or Rishikesh and Nainital (a full day by road). Alternatively, return to Delhi between the two by train and start the second route fresh.

sections.heading: Extensions
list: Munsiyari: add two days from Kausani for the Panchachuli view.
Chopta and Tungnath: add two days from Rishikesh for an easy trek.
Lansdowne: a quiet night on the way from Delhi.
Jim Corbett: combine with Nainital for a safari.

sections.heading: Getting there
list: Delhi to Dehradun or Haridwar by Shatabdi or Vande Bharat for Garhwal.
Delhi to Kathgodam by Shatabdi for Kumaon.
Pantnagar and Dehradun have airports with limited flights.
Hire a car and driver locally for the hill sections.

sections.heading: Where to stay
paras: In Mussoorie, Landour and the Camel's Back Road end are quieter than the Library Chowk end of the Mall. In Kumaon, Bhimtal or Sattal are calmer lake bases than Nainital, and Mukteshwar, Kausani and Binsar have small resorts and heritage bungalows with views. Binsar's stays are inside the sanctuary and simple, with limited electricity.

sections.heading: Season notes
list: March to April: rhododendrons in bloom across Kumaon.
May to June: busy in Mussoorie and Nainital; book early.
October to December: the clearest Himalayan views of the year.
January to February: cold; snow is possible at Mussoorie, Dhanaulti, Mukteshwar and Binsar.

sections.heading: Food to try
list: Kumaoni bhatt ki churkani (black soybean curry) and aloo ke gutke.
Bal mithai and singori, Almora's sweets.

safety: Drive times are approximate and depend on traffic, weather, landslides and road works; allow extra time and avoid driving after dark.
Permits, e-passes, ropeways and pass openings change; check official portals before you travel.
In the monsoon, check the state disaster-management updates before driving.
packing: Layers and a warm jacket for October to February

faqs.q: How many days do I need for Uttarakhand's hill stations?
faqs.a: Five days for Garhwal, seven for Kumaon, or about 12 for both.

faqs.q: Which is better, Mussoorie or Nainital?
faqs.a: Mussoorie suits walkers and views; Nainital suits families with its lake. Both are busy in summer.

faqs.q: Where can I see the Himalaya best in Kumaon?
faqs.a: Kausani, Binsar, Mukteshwar and Munsiyari in clear weather, especially from October to December.

faqs.q: Can I combine Rishikesh with Mussoorie?
faqs.a: Yes, easily; they are about two hours apart by road.

faqs.q: Can I do the Kumaon loop by public transport?
faqs.a: Buses and shared taxis connect the towns, but a hired car saves a lot of time and allows sunrise and sunset stops.
